subject: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Patel <emma@veridian.ai>, Amit Desai <amit@veridian.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP

Hi Emma / Amit —

Thanks for taking the time today — great convo. Quick recap of the performance items we committed to clarify during the demo and the lightweight pilot we suggest to validate SLOs in your environment. Please confirm or correct anything below.

SLO targets you mentioned as goals:
- Latency: target 95th percentile per-token generation p95 <= 150ms at steady-state for single-request (non-streaming) workloads.
- Streaming: first byte streaming latency <= 200ms (initial partial response) and steady per-token latency <= 120ms when streaming enabled.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrent connections ~120 max, with short bursts to 300 for 2–4 minutes.
- Throughput: expected sustained tokens/sec aggregate ~18k tokens/sec during peak windows (peak 22k).

Key constraints you flagged:
- Encrypted KV cache required (customer-managed KMS) for any cached prompts.
- Internal compliance: audit logs retained 90 days.

Proposed pilot (MAP) — phased and measurable:
1) Baseline benchmark: Redwood runs a controlled load test against a sandbox model variant (we bring 2 identical endpoints) to validate p95 numbers and streaming first-byte.
2) Integration run: Veridian imports an anonymized 24-hr production traffic sample (no PII) so we can replay and measure realistic latencies/throughput.
3) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 180ms for non-streaming, streaming first-byte <= 220ms for 95% of requests, <2% error rate, and sustained system throughput within 15% of your peak forecast.

Action items (proposed owners / dates):
- Veridian: share anonymized traffic sample + any concurrency throttles (Amit) — due Sep 8.
- Redwood: deliver baseline benchmark report + SLO checklist (Ben / Soojin) — due Sep 9.
- CS/Eng: confirm KMS integration steps & retention config (Monica) — Sep 11.

Attachments: SLO checklist and demo perf logs referenced below.

Please reply if these look correct and we’ll lock dates. If you prefer, we can push the baseline test earlier next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-checklist.xlsx (14 KB)]
[Attachment: veridian_demo_perf_log_20280905.zip (2.3 MB)]

From: Emma Patel <emma@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@veridian.ai>, eng-ops@veridian.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and captures most of what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 120 concurrent connections is what our frontend regularly opens; each connection typically generates ~1.8 requests per second during high interactivity. Bursts to 300 happen roughly twice/day, lasting up to 3 minutes.
- For streaming first byte, we actually need 95th <= 180ms rather than 200ms to be safe for our UX. Can Redwood validate at that tighter bound?
- On KMS: we can provide customer-managed keys in the sandbox (Amit will coordinate).

We will pull together an anonymized 48-hour sample (no PII) and drop it in the Drive folder you shared by Sep 8 EOD. We also want the baseline report to include tokenization characteristics (avg tokens per request) so we can map cost.

If Redwood can confirm the revised streaming first-byte target (95th <= 180ms) as achievable in the pilot acceptance criteria, we’ll proceed.

—Emma
VP Product, Veridian Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Patel <emma@veridian.ai>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit@veridian.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP

Thanks Emma — we can absolutely target the tighter streaming first-byte p95 <= 180ms for the pilot. A few implementation notes so expectations are aligned:

- We’ll run two variants in parallel during the baseline: a quantized LLM variant (lower cost) and a full-precision variant so you can compare latency and quality.
- Streaming latency is sensitive to client chunking. For the replay, please indicate whether you use small chunk sizes (~64 tokens) or larger (~256 tokens). That will materially affect first-byte performance.
- For the anonymized replay, please include a short README with average tokens per request and any special prompting (function calls, long contexts).

Proposed next steps:
- Veridian uploads the sample + README to the Drive folder by EOD Sep 8.
- Redwood schedules baseline benchmark and shares report by Sep 9 morning PST.
- Plan a joint 60-min review on Sep 10 to go over results and decide on Dedicated vs Hosted sizing for your peak windows.

I’ll create the MAP in HubSpot and invite the key owners. Thanks for moving fast on this.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7842]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP

Internal: technical checklist and ops notes for the baseline run (action owners assigned).

Notes:
- Sandbox topology: we’ll spin two fleet groups in us-west2 with identical configs except quantization flags. Expect ~4 VMs (A100 equivalent) per variant for initial run; can scale to 6 if sustained throughput requires.
- KV cache: enable encrypted prefix cache with CMK; need Karthik to confirm KMS ARNs by Sept 9.
- Telemetry: enable request tracing + token-level latency breakdowns; we must capture first-byte timestamps for streaming. Store traces in the shared Drive folder as ndjson.
- Error handling: set retry policy to 2 retries for 503/504 during replay and capture retry counts in report.

Action items:
- Soojin: prep benchmark harness and sample replay script, target Sep 9 06:00 PST baseline start.
- Karthik: confirm KMS parameters and check compliance note for 90-day retention — Sep 9 EOD.
- Ben: confirm HubSpot MAP owners and loop in legal for any pilot data agreement.

I’ll attach the internal test checklist to the MAP.

-Monica
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal_benchmark_checklist.pdf (9 KB)]

From: Amit Desai <amit@veridian.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Emma Patel <emma@veridian.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@veridian.ai, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming & concurrency recap + proposed pilot MAP

Thanks all — we uploaded the 48-hour anonymized sample and a short README to the Drive folder (link above). README includes: avg tokens/request = 78, typical chunking = 128 tokens, and a note that ~8% of requests use function-calls with structured JSON responses.

We confirm KMS ARNs will be provided by EOD Sep 9. Sep 9 baseline start time at 06:00 PST works for our ops team.

One ask from procurement: if the pilot shows we meet your acceptance criteria, can you share a rough Dedicated sizing estimate (monthly) so we can budget ahead of the Sep 20 exec review? A ballpark is fine.

Emma/Amit — feel free to call if anything needs faster clarification.

—Amit
SRE Lead, Veridian Health
[Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-veridian-pilot]
